units.deviation: Same rule: size, then HTML sniff, then hashes; a mismatch discards the file instead of installing it. The new code also hashes the resume-skip path before committing.

units.deviation: Downloads still stream into a `.part` sibling, verify, then rename atomically; a cancelled or failed transfer leaves the `.part` for resume rather than a half-written jar.
units.evidence: client.rs module doc (lines 4-5) states `.part` siblings then verify then atomic commit; the open path at 802 is the F-038 guard and the commit happens after verify_and_commit; the old download_manager.py writes `.part` at 312 and keeps it on cancel at 393.

units.spec_id: F-041 / F-042 reject path traversal and absolute paths
units.deviation: The Rust side delegates the name check to zip's enclosed_name(), which rejects absolute paths, drive prefixes and `..` in one call, and additionally caps the joined path length at extraction.
units.evidence: inspect.rs:122 rejects any member whose file.enclosed_name() is None; extract.rs:19 caps MAX_JOINED_PATH_LEN at 260 and extract.rs:123 refuses longer targets; the old inspect_zip_members (safe_archive.py:108) applies the same rule via safe_archive_member_name.

units.spec_id: F-038 / F-044 refuse symlinks and special files
units.deviation: Symlinks are refused at both ends: the download destination is checked after open and before write (the Windows race the old app guarded), and archive members that are links or special files are rejected during inspection.
units.evidence: client.rs:802 documents the F-038 guard that re-checks the opened path; test spec_f038_a_symlink_at_the_destination_is_refused (client.rs:1558) proves a symlink at the destination is refused end to end; the old artifact_verifier.py:84 refuses path.is_symlink() before hashing.

units.spec_id: F-043 archive size, count and ratio limits
units.deviation: Limits exist and are enforced before any write: 50,000 members, 4 GiB per member, 32 GiB total uncompressed, and a 500:1 ratio above a 1 MiB floor. The ratio rule is a pure function so it is unit-tested without a zip.
units.evidence: ArchiveLimits defaults at inspect.rs:32-36; inspect_zip checks max_members at 107, max_member_size at 141, running total at 146 and ratio_rejected at 148; ratio_rejected is defined at 89; test spec_f043_extract_enforces_limits_before_any_write (extract.rs:348); old ArchiveLimits at safe_archive.py:27-32 with the ratio rule at 147-153.

units.deviation: The filename is still the source of truth: a mod is disabled when it ends in `.jar.disabled` or lives under a `disabled_mods/` segment, and the scan reads both spellings so the state survives a toggle without a database flag.
units.evidence: instances/mod.rs:110-111 accepts both suffixes, is_disabled_path at 118 checks the suffix and the disabled_mods segment at 130, and the scan pushes disabled_mods/ at 161; the old toggle in profile_content_toggle.py performs the same rename with preview and undo.

units.deviation: Redaction is fail-closed: a value that cannot be classified becomes `<REDACTED:unavailable>` rather than passing through, and report writing aborts on a sanitiser error instead of writing an unsanitised line.
units.evidence: sanitize.rs:42 defines UNAVAILABLE and 75-83 the REDACTED_* placeholders; report.rs:26-30 maps a SanitizeError to a ReportError::Sanitize and report.rs:66-88 sanitises every line before writing; the old log_sanitizer.py:13-21 and its _SENSITIVE_FIELD_REPLACEMENTS table at 24 do the same.

units.deviation: Two separate sets, never one: PRESENT is what the scan found on disk, ELIGIBLE is the lock entries that have a file. A file present but absent from the lock is UNKNOWN and always kept, which is the data-loss bug lessons.md §4.2 records.
units.evidence: target.rs:7-14 states the two-set rule and that UNKNOWN is always kept; present_files and eligible_files are separate fields at 194-197; the split is computed at 316-320 and 417-418; entry_is_present at 758 matches lock entries to facts and counts both disabled spellings.

units.deviation: Pruning is still a dry-run first: preview_lock_prune returns candidates plus a digest, the UI shows them, and execute_lock_prune must echo the digest; files the lock never recorded are kept, matching the old sync-prune checkbox semantics.
units.evidence: target.rs:774 documents that present files no lock entry claims are returned separately and kept; preview_lock_prune returns { candidates, dryRun: true, presentFiles, lockEntries, digest } and execute_lock_prune refuses a stale digest; the old main_window.py:2552 exposes the same choice as «Remove saved profile entries not found in this scan (metadata only)».

units.spec_id: F-080 / F-113 double verification by token and manifest digest
units.deviation: A plan is bound to the state it was built from: update installs carry a token derived from the lock digest and target, and a restore carries the manifest SHA-256; both are re-checked immediately before writing and refused when stale.
units.evidence: apply.rs:198-205 defines PlanContext with the token, apply.rs:474 check_context re-reads digest, target and folder state before the write, and apply.rs:541 derives the token; backup/restore.rs:84 carries manifest_sha256, restore.rs:179 computes it, and restore.rs:430 refuses when the manifest no longer matches the plan; the old mrpack_installer.py:136/181/189 binds an install to manifest_sha256.

units.deviation: No measurement artifact exists for the new app: there is no benches/ directory, no criterion or divan in Cargo.toml, and no built binary to time. The budget is recorded (2.1 s → ≤1.0 s) but nothing proves it.
units.evidence: Test-Path benches returned False and Cargo.toml/core/Cargo.toml contain no criterion/divan/bench target; the only startup-adjacent code is db::open (db/mod.rs:198-217), which sets busy_timeout, gates the schema version and asserts WAL before any write; that is design evidence, not a timing.

units.deviation: Same blocker as B-1: the 6.2 s → ≤3.0 s budget cannot be measured without a built app and a repeat-run harness; nothing in the repo records a warm-start number.
units.evidence: No bench target and no measurement file anywhere under core/ or src-tauri/; preferences.applyToDocument (preferences.ts:80-85) settles theme, lang and dir before first paint, which is intended to avoid a flash rather than to cut startup time, so it does not discharge the budget.

units.deviation: Memory is not measured. The old number came from PowerShell/Win32 counters on the PySide process; the new app is a WebView2 host, so the old process boundary does not even apply and no equivalent counter was run.
units.evidence: No memory harness in the repo (no scripts/ and no bench crate); the baseline table is baseline.md:48-51 (194.3 MB median) and performance-budgets.md §5 already warns that the WebView2 memory is not comparable to the Qt process; verdict stays unverifiable rather than claiming a pass.

units.deviation: Same as B-3 for PrivateBytes: no counter was collected for the Tauri host, and the budget is a Qt-process figure that performance-budgets.md §5 says must be re-derived, not copied.
units.evidence: baseline.md:48-51 records 111.3 MB median PrivateBytes for the Python app; there is no measurement run, no profiling script and no target/debug build in the repo, so there is nothing to compare.

units.spec_id: B-5 cold scan of 354 jars ≤ 960 ms
units.deviation: The scan path exists (top-level entries plus disabled_mods/, jar metadata read per file) but was never timed on the 354-jar fixture; the 1922 ms → ≤960 ms budget is unproven.
units.evidence: instances/mod.rs:135-161 defines the scan roots and core/src/jar_reader/loader.rs reads each jar; no fixture of 354 jars and no timing harness exist in the repo (no benches/, no criterion); baseline.md:59 records 1922.1 ms on the old app.

units.spec_id: B-6 warm scan of 354 jars ≤ 540 ms
units.deviation: A warm-scan cache keyed on (path, size, mtime) exists and an unchanged jar is never re-opened, which is the mechanism B-6 needs, but no timing proves it reaches 540 ms.
units.evidence: jar_reader/cache.rs:1-3 documents the (path,size,mtime) key and cache.rs:23-40 returns a hit without opening the jar; there is no benchmark and no 354-jar fixture, so the 1080 ms → ≤540 ms target remains unmeasured.

units.deviation: The old 4.2 ms measured reading installed_mods.json; the new app stores installed mods in SQLite, so the baseline does not map one-to-one and the remaining manifest reader is the backup manifest, which was never timed.
units.evidence: Installed mods live in the installed_mods table (core/src/db/schema.rs:17, written at core/src/db/mod.rs:400); the JSON manifest reader that remains is read_manifest at backup/manifest.rs:238 and manifest_digest at 304, with no timing; baseline.md:62 records 4.2 ms for the old JSON manifest.
